p.title: Meera's mango tree
p.challenge: Put the events of the story in order. What is its moral?
panels: Meera wanted the best mangoes in the village.
Kabir said, "Buy a magic powder and the tree will fruit overnight!"
Meera shook her head.
Every morning she watered her tree, pulled weeds and added compost.
Two summers later, her tree gave sweet, golden mangoes.
She shared the mangoes with everyone.

p.title: The myna and the jackal
p.challenge: Put the events of the fable in order
panels: A myna sat upon a tree with a roti held tight in her beak.
A jackal called, "O bird so fair, your song must be a pure delight!"
She sang out loud, and the roti fell.
The jackal grabbed it and ran out of sight.
Now Myna knows that honeyed words can hide a plan.

p.title: Dadaji's spectacles
p.challenge: Put the events of the funny tale in order
panels: At a busy railway station, a cheeky monkey snatched Dadaji's spectacles.
It leapt onto the roof of a tea stall.
People shouted and waved, but the monkey only chattered.
Little Lata stayed calm and held up a banana.
Plop! The monkey dropped the spectacles into Dadaji's lap.
Everyone laughed and clapped.

p.title: Tara and Bholu
p.challenge: Put the story in order. How do Tara's feelings change?

"We have nothing in common," Tara grumbled.
Tara hurt her ankle and had to sit at home for a week.
Bholu came over and taught her to paint the sunset.
On Sports Day, Tara cheered louder than anyone for nervous Bholu.

Now Akbar's line looked shorter!

p.title: The old chair
p.challenge: The chair tells its own story. Put the events in order.
panels: I am an old wooden chair on Nani's verandah.
For forty years I have held visitors, grandchildren and one very fat cat.
My legs creak now, and someone said, "Let's throw it away."
Little Chintu painted my arms blue and said, "You're my throne!"
I felt young again.

The bus, a beetle, makes no noise.

How tiny all their worries seem
When seen from up among the clouds,
Where every road is like a dream.

Nani made him warm milk with a pinch of haldi.

p.title: The kabaddi final
p.challenge: Put the story in order. What was Sana's change of heart?

The rival captain, Divya, slipped and twisted her ankle.
"Keep going! Now we'll win easily!" shouted Sana's teammates.
Sana stopped, helped Divya up and called for the first-aid kit.
Sana's team lost by two points, yet the crowd clapped for her.

At twenty-five, she gave her first concert.
Today she teaches music to children who are blind.

p.title: A visit to the National War Memorial
p.challenge: Put the class visit in order

A golden flame burned quietly at the centre.
Around it, rings of granite walls carried thousands of names.
We walked slowly and spoke in whispers.
"Each name belongs to a soldier who gave their life for our country," said our teacher.
